issue.title: Hibernate Reactive thread model fixes

labels.name: area/dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

issue.body:
- Changed `Mutiny.Session Panache.getSession` to `Uni<Mutiny.Session> Panache.getSession`
- Changed `boolean PanacheEntity.isPersistent` to `Uni<Boolean> PanacheEntity.isPersistent`
- Added `@ReactiveTransaction` to forward to `Mutiny.Session.withTransaction`: method must return a `Uni` or be invoked from a non-`VertxThread` (in which case it blocks)
- Make sure we create `Mutiny.Session` objects from the right threads
- Still rely on the request-scoped `Mutiny.Session` and not the Vert.x context one used by `Mutiny.Session.withSession`
- Added `Panache.currentTransaction` which forwards to `Mutiny.Session.currentTransaction`
- Added a guide
- Fixed a mocking issue wrt interfaces

@Sanne @gavinking this should resolve the issues we've been having, right?

issue.title: Hibernate Reactive withSession() breaks named queries & context after hot reload
issue.body:
## Describe the bug
When using HR's `sessionFactory.withSession()` or `withTransaction()`, a hot reload of the application will lead to various problems. For example, named queries will stop working (similar to #15164) or accessing an injected SecurityContext will trigger NullPointerExceptions.

### Expected behavior
Using HR `withSession()` behaves nicely and does not break the application after any changes and subsequent hot reload.

### Actual behavior
Using HR `withSession()` will break various things in the application once a hot reload is triggered. For example, executing a NamedQuery will throw:

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Type specified for TypedQuery [com.example.Fruit] is incompatible with query return type [class com.example.Fruit]
	at org.hibernate.internal.AbstractSharedSessionContract.resultClassChecking(AbstractSharedSessionContract.java:878)
	at org.hibernate.reactive.session.impl.ReactiveSessionImpl.createReactiveQuery(ReactiveSessionImpl.java:510)
	at org.hibernate.reactive.session.impl.ReactiveSessionImpl.buildReactiveQueryFromName(ReactiveSessionImpl.java:487)
	at org.hibernate.reactive.session.impl.ReactiveSessionImpl.createReactiveNamedQuery(ReactiveSessionImpl.java:472)
	at org.hibernate.reactive.mutiny.impl.MutinySessionImpl.createNamedQuery(MutinySessionImpl.java:251)
	at com.example.FruitResource.lambda$getFruits$0(FruitResource.java:33)
	...
```

Similarly, an injected SecurityContext will stop working:

```

```


## To Reproduce

Link to a small reproducer: https://github.com/markusdlugi/hibernate-reactive-hot-reload

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Start application
2. Execute some query, e.g. `POST http://localhost:8080/fruit` or `GET http://localhost:8080/fruit`. Everything should still be working.
3. Change something in the application, e.g. remove line 33 in `FruitResource`.
4. Issue another request `GET http://localhost:8080/fruit`. The application will start hot reloading and then throw an exception when executing the NamedQuery.

### Configuration
See reproducer, no special config is required to trigger this behavior.

### Screenshots

## Environment (please complete the following information):

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`
Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.18363.1556]

### Output of `java -version`
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM Corretto-11.0.10.9.1 (build 11.0.10+9-LTS, mixed mode)

### GraalVM version (if different from Java)
N/A

### Quarkus version or git rev
2.0.0.Final

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)
Apache Maven 3.6.3

## Additional context
The problems do _not_ appear when injecting `Mutiny.Session` (i.e. using the `ReactiveSessionProducer`) instead of using `withSession()`. But that will in turn trigger other problems (see #18268).

body: I think you linked to this issue instead of the duplicate one
@stuartwdouglas would you be able to look at this? If not I can try myself, but not before next week.

So this will work if you do `-Dvertx.disableTCCL=true` (although you get a heap of warnings in the logs). The fundamental issue here is that vert.x hangs onto the original TCCL, and we can't update it. With Vert.x 3 we had a hack that allowed us to modify the TCCL, however this is no longer working as the Vert.x Context explicitly sets the TCCL to the old CL for every operation.

Hi @stuartwdouglas, thanks a lot for the insights! I can confirm that setting `-Dvertx.disableTCCL=true` will fix the issue, named queries will work again. Do you know whether this can have any other negative side effects, or is this a safe workaround (other than printing out a lot of warnings)?

Besides that, any idea how we could fix this properly? I still find it interesting that this happens if you use `sessionFactory.withSession()` but not if you inject `Mutiny.Session`. Is it due to the former making use of the Vert.x Context for storing the session? Do we need to ensure that any sessions are removed from the context upon reload?

As a side note, I noticed that the other problem I described in #18301 that an injected `SecurityContext` stops working actually happens regardless of hot reload. So once you try to access a `SecurityContext` within a `withSession()` block you get the mentioned error, no matter if the application was reloaded or not. Therefore, that issue is also not fixed by setting `-Dvertx.disableTCCL=true`. So that might be another issue unrelated to the TCCL issue that causes named queries to fail.
